trust_decision.summary: Trusted as a real, single-commit published fix for a genuine flaw: at the pinned commit ConfigMerge copies source keys straight into the target, and for a key named '__proto__' the target's inherited Object.prototype is itself accepted as a plain object by isPlainObject, so the merge recurses into Object.prototype and writes there; Jodit.configure is a public entry point into exactly that. The fix adds one shared key filter inside both ConfigMerge and ConfigProto. Scope is thin: the ConfigProto site is behaviourally indistinguishable before and after the fix, so the only additional testable route is the untouched public path-writer set().

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names ConfigMerge explicitly and Jodit.configure forwards straight to it (src/jodit.ts:257); ConfigMerge:151-155 is the recursive write that reaches Object.prototype, so this is the first correct place to read after the summary.

fix_sites.entry_point: Jodit.configure() (src/jodit.ts:256-258, public static API) and Jodit.modules.Helpers.ConfigMerge (exported via src/modules/index.ts:14,30)
fix_sites.module_kind: core helper / in-place config merge, reached from a public static API and from the public helper namespace

fix_sites.entry_point: Jodit.make()/new Jodit(..., options) -> initOptions (src/jodit.ts:1221-1224) and Jodit.modules.Helpers.ConfigProto; also every component that merges its own options (src/core/view/view.ts:298-302, src/modules/uploader/uploader.ts:300-306, src/core/request/ajax.ts:51-54, src/modules/dialog/dialog.ts:709-711, src/modules/file-browser/file-browser.ts:363)
fix_sites.module_kind: second merge implementation / defaults-or-merge route (prototype-chain variant used at editor creation)

fix_sites.entry_point: n/a - new shared predicate isUnsafeProtoKey + UNSAFE_PROTO_KEYS list used by both merge functions

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/core/helpers/utils/config-proto.ts:51-100 (ConfigProto - the prototype-chain merge used at editor creation)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: An engineer can fix only the function the advisory names (ConfigMerge, reached from Jodit.configure) and argue ConfigProto is a different, prototype-chain-based mechanism: it only assigns __proto__ onto a fresh object which is then overwritten by Object.setPrototypeOf (config-proto.ts:97), so by itself it cannot touch Object.prototype.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: ConfigProto's documented prototype-chain fallback and Jodit.atom() atomic replacement must keep working: partial nested options inherit untouched defaults through the object prototype, and values wrapped with Jodit.atom() (non-enumerable isAtom flag) replace instead of merge. A fix that deep-clones/JSON-round-trips the merge, or skips every key that also exists on the target's prototype chain, drops inherited defaults, functions and the isAtom marker and breaks the existing two-level controls-merge test.

O6_input_shapes: An own '__proto__' key produced by JSON.parse (not by an object literal), nested at least one level under an existing plain-object option such as 'controls' - this is the shape that actually reaches Object.prototype; the advisory example uses it (fix.diff:26-39)

A bare top-level '__proto__' key is NOT the global path through Jodit.configure: target[key] resolves to Config.prototype, which isPlainObject rejects (src/config.ts:1165-1167, src/core/helpers/checker/is-plain-object.ts:25-28), so the write only changes defaultOptions' own prototype

A 'constructor' -> 'prototype' chain (fix.diff:41-53) and a bare 'prototype' key (fix.diff:90) - the fix filters them, but on a plain target they only create own local properties, so these shapes do not by themselves mutate Object.prototype
Any nesting depth, because the filter runs inside the recursive forEach of both merge functions, not once at the entry point

Not a shape the fix needs or handles: array-wrapped payloads (ConfigMerge replaces arrays instead of recursing, config-proto.ts:151-155) and object-literal {__proto__: ...} input, which creates no own key at all

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Jodit.modules.Helpers.set(chain, value, obj) writes the last dotted segment into obj; a '__proto__' segment resolves to Object.prototype (isPlainObject accepts it and isArray rejects it, set.ts:43), so set('__proto__.polluted', 'yes', {}) mutates Object.prototype globally - and this public helper is jodit's own way of writing nested option values
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The dotted chain is developer-supplied (the in-tree callers pass fixed literals such as file-browser/data-provider.ts:347), so an engineer can argue this is a path-writer, not configuration merging, and outside the advisory's property.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: 1 file from the fix, same src/core/helpers/utils directory; exported as a public helper (src/core/helpers/utils/index.ts:35, src/modules/index.ts:30, listed in src/jodit.test.js:195)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A path-writer helper that takes its dotted chain from external data instead of a literal
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The helper is already documented and used as the public way to write nested option values (Jodit.modules.Helpers.set, called with a path into this.options at src/modules/file-browser/data-provider.ts:347), so a config-import or deep-link feature would naturally pass a caller-supplied path.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Copying every key of a server JSON item onto a shared cache/defaults object instead of onto the item instance
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: File-browser items arrive as remote JSON (data-provider.ts:116-119) and the constructor already copies keys blindly; a maintainer adding a per-source item cache or a defaults object for item fields would reuse the same loop with a shared target.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A JSON-round-trip store that writes a caller-supplied key into a module-level or shared config object rather than a freshly parsed root
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This provider already parses a JSON root object and writes json[key] = value with a caller-controlled key (line 61-63); a persisted-settings variant keeping one root object for all editors would turn the same line into prototype pollution.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Building observable accessors from the keys of an option sub-object taken straight from user config
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Observable objects are created from arbitrary option objects (synces), and initAccessors copies each key into a local store and redefines it on the dict; a nested-observable change would run it over user-supplied option trees.

O9_family: prototype pollution in recursive configuration merge (CWE-1321)

O10_build.toolchain: npm + make (cross-platform Makefile delegating to make.js), webpack 5 with tsx/swc loaders, TypeScript 6; tests via karma + mocha + chai in a headless browser (npm test -> make test browsers=chrome_headless)
O10_build.project_tests: src/core/helpers/helpers.test.js: ConfigProto/ConfigFlatten/ConfigDeepFlatten suite (599-818), ConfigMerge suite (820-915), Jodit.configure suite (917-1067); the pollution tests added by the fix (fix.diff:26-39, 41-53, 61-72) are absent at the pinned commit

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Filter or delete unsafe keys once at the top of Jodit.configure() (or guard only the top level of ConfigMerge's source before looping): the advisory payload is nested under 'controls', so the recursion still reaches Object.prototype, and nothing is added at the untouched public path-writer set().

out_of_scope_notes: The fixed commit also edits CHANGELOG.md and test/loader.js (adds src/plugins/select-cells/select-cells.test.js to the karma case list) - release/test plumbing, not part of the security fix.

Components reach ConfigProto with their own constructor options (src/core/view/view.ts:298-302 and the overrides listed in fix_sites); these are caller entry points I folded into O1's editor-creation entry point rather than counting separately.
